Successive-difference replicate weights for a chromy sample

Source: R/variance.R
as_svrepdesign.Rd

Builds a replicate-weights design in the successive difference replication scheme of Fay and Train (1995), the convention of the American Community Survey: the rows whose selection was actually random are perturbed, in list order, by factors 1 +- 2^(-3/2) * 2 read off pairs of rows of a Hadamard matrix, so that the replicate variance approximates the successive-difference variance of estimate_total() while giving the survey package's whole replicate machinery — quantiles, domains, calibration — a design to work with. Rows selected with certainty keep their weight in every replicate, as they carry no variance.

Usage

as_svrepdesign(x, replicates = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A chromy_sample().

replicates

The number of replicates, or NULL for the smallest Hadamard order above the number of randomly selected rows.

...

Passed on to survey::svrepdesign().

Value

A svyrep.design object with scale 4 / replicates.

References

Fay, R. E. and Train, G. F. (1995). Aspects of survey and model-based postcensal estimation of income and poverty characteristics for states and counties. Proceedings of the ASA, Government Statistics Section, 154–159.

Examples

set.seed(11)
frame <- data.frame(size = rlnorm(120, 2), y = rlnorm(120, 4))
s <- chromy_sample(frame, n = 30, size = "size")
r <- as_svrepdesign(s)
survey::svytotal(~y, r)
#>   total     SE
#> y 13671 4124.2
estimate_total(s, "y")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   variable  total    se cv_pct random_draws
#>   <chr>     <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 y        13671. 4188.   30.6           27
